architecture.approach: Port the hookgate crate from feature/m3-substrate as prior art and adapt it to the current workspace: one library crate at crates/hookgate, feature-gated with default = [presets] and an additive presets feature that ships the provider verifiers. The core is four value types (DeliveryId, IdempotencyKey, InboundRequest, VerifiedEvent) plus DeliveryRecord, InsertOutcome, and DeadLetterRecord, a redacting error type, and three traits: Verifier (synchronous, because signature checking does no I/O), DeliveryStore, and Outbox (both async). The load-bearing invariant is that verification runs over the exact received bytes; InboundRequest therefore holds Bytes and never a parsed document, and the module docs state that re-serialization is a security bug. MemoryDeliveryStore is the reference implementation. The crate has no provider client, no outbound HTTP, no HTTP server, and no axum integration, and it depends on platform-core only for tenant identity.

dataModel.flowDescription: A verified request follows one path: receive the raw bytes, resolve the tenant and provider, verify the signature against those exact bytes with a constant-time comparison, reject a timestamp outside the tolerance as stale, insert the delivery if it is new, enqueue the verified event to the outbox, and only then report success. A duplicate insert returns InsertOutcome::Duplicate rather than a second row, and uniqueness includes the tenant so the same event id from two tenants is not a duplicate. The processor consumes the outbox, marks the delivery processed, or dead-letters it with the raw body and reason. Replay of a dead-lettered delivery is idempotent against the delivery store.

securityConsiderations.description: Every delivery read and write is scoped by tenant; another tenant cannot observe or replay a delivery that is not theirs.
Signature material and shared secrets never render: the error type is redacted and InboundRequest holds raw bytes without a secret field.
Headers, raw bodies, and event ids are validated and bounded before use; an oversized or malformed request is a typed error rather than a panic.
The crate reads no secret from the environment; the caller constructs each verifier with its own secret.

performanceConsiderations.strategy: Signature comparison is constant-time (subtle) so verification cost does not leak the expected value through timing.
InboundRequest keeps the body as Bytes and clones by reference counting, so the raw bytes are not copied per verification stage.

risks.description: The raw-body rule is easy to violate by a well-meaning refactor that parses first, which silently breaks every signature.
risks.mitigation: AC-001 and AC-003 assert it directly and EC-001 names the failure so a test can pin it.

risks.description: The delivery-and-outbox-before-acknowledge guarantee is weak when the two writes are not transactional in the memory store.
risks.mitigation: State the guarantee explicitly on the store contract and pin it with AC-007 and EC-003.

risks.description: Porting stale code may drag in a cross-crate dev-dependency on quota-ledger from the prior art.
risks.mitigation: Declare dependencies directly and drop the cross-crate dev-dependency unless the test actually needs it.
